transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, hi. I guess I’ve just been feeling really worn out most days. It’s probably not a huge thing, but even when I get a full night’s sleep, I wake up feeling like my body and my head are still kind of dragging, especially when I have to go in for my cashier shift. I wasn’t sure if that’s something worth coming in for, but it’s been happening a lot.
How long have you been feeling this way?

I guess it’s been… longer than I wanted to admit, maybe about a year and three months. It kind of started after our older relative moved in with us. I mean, it hasn’t been awful every single day, but yeah, around then is when I started noticing it.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like, or has that changed over the past year or so?

Um… I’m not totally sure. I mean, I still do enjoy things when I actually get around to them, I think. Maybe I haven’t paid super close attention to whether that’s changed. It’s not like everything feels pointless or anything like that. Is that what you mean?
When you do get around to doing things you used to enjoy, do you feel as much pleasure from them as you used to?

I think so, yeah. Like, if I actually sit down and watch something I like or spend time doing something fun, I can still enjoy it. Maybe I’m a little distracted sometimes, but I wouldn’t say the pleasure is gone or anything. Is that… the kind of thing you’re asking?
Have you been having any thoughts about being a burden to others, feeling worthless, or wishing you weren't alive?
Um… I don’t think so. I mean, I feel bad sometimes if I’m stressing people out, but I wouldn’t say I feel worthless or like I don’t want to be alive. Nothing like that, no. Is that okay to say?
Have you been feeling nervous or on edge a lot of the time lately?

Yeah… I guess I have been kind of on edge. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but my mind jumps around a lot—like money stuff, the relative staying with us, my wife being stressed, church responsibilities, and then whether I’m messing things up at work. It’s just… a lot of little things, I guess. Does that make sense?
Have you been feeling consistently down or depressed most of the time over the past year?

I don’t think so… not consistently, no. I have rough days where I feel kind of worn down or discouraged, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been depressed most of the time for a whole year. I hope that answers it the right way.
When you are doing things you normally enjoy, do you feel less interested in them than you used to?
I don’t think so, not really. I mean, I still like the things I usually like… maybe I get distracted sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest in them or anything. Is that what you mean?
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past year?
Not really, no. I mean, my weight goes up and down a little like anyone’s, but I haven’t noticed anything significant over the past year. At least nothing that stood out to me.
Do you feel like you're looking forward to things less often than you used to?

I don’t think so… I mean, I still look forward to things, like days off or seeing people. Maybe I don’t get super excited every time, but I wouldn’t say it’s less than it used to be. I hope that makes sense.
Do you often feel sad or empty inside?
Not really… I mean, I have off days like anyone, but I wouldn’t say I often feel sad or empty inside. I don’t think that’s a big thing for me, if that makes sense.
Do you feel like you're having less fun or enjoying things less than you used to, even when you're doing activities that are normally pleasurable?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I still enjoy things when I’m doing them… watching something, spending time with someone, that kind of thing. Maybe I’m not always totally relaxed, but I wouldn’t say I’m having less fun than I used to. Is that what you mean?
Do you often find it difficult to concentrate or make decisions?

Sometimes, yeah… not all the time, but it happens. Like at the register, I can be looking right at the screen and still kind of lose track because I’m thinking about stuff at home or bills. Then I have to recount the drawer or catch a small mistake. It’s not constant, but it does happen enough that I notice it. Does that make sense?
Do you have days where you feel completely fine and your mood is normal?

Yeah, I think so. I mean, I do have days where my mood feels pretty normal and I’m not… down or anything. Maybe I still get a little in my head sometimes, but overall, yes, I’d say I have normal days. Is that kind of what you’re asking?
Have you had at least two years where you felt down or depressed for most of the day, even if it wasn't every single day?

No, I don’t think so. I’ve had stretches where I felt stressed or kind of worn down, but not like two years of being depressed most of the day. At least, I wouldn’t describe it that way. Is that what you mean?
Do you feel like you need to push yourself to get interested in or enjoy activities that you normally like?

I don’t think so, not really. I mean, if I’m tired I might put things off a little, but I wouldn’t say I have to force myself to enjoy things I normally like. Once I’m doing them, it’s usually fine. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you had a period of at least two weeks where you felt depressed or down most of the day?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I’ve had bad days or maybe a few days where I felt kind of low, but not like two weeks straight where I was down most of the day. At least not that I can remember. Is that okay—like, is that what you’re asking?
Have you had more than two months where you felt depressed or down most of the day?
No, I don’t think so. I’ve had times where I felt kind of down or tired of things, but not more than two months where it was most of the day. At least, I don’t remember it being like that.
Would you say your feelings of being worn out and on edge have been interfering with your daily life a lot, a little, or not at all?

Maybe a little. I’m still getting through the day, but I have noticed I’m double-checking my cash drawer more than I used to because I’ll make small mistakes, and that bothers me. And I’ve kind of cut back on volunteering at the food pantry, just because I don’t feel like I can keep up with everything as well right now. It’s not like everything’s falling apart, but… yeah, I guess it’s interfering some.
Have you felt this way for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

I’m not totally sure… I don’t think it’s been most of the day nearly every day for two weeks. I mean, I’ve had stretches where I feel on edge or worn out, but it’s not constant all day. I hope that answers it right.
